7segment.name: 7 Segment
7segment.notes: 7-segment display: every segment (A-G, DP) needs its own 220-470 ohm resistor, and the common pin (COM.1/COM.2, or CLN/COM on the 4-digit module) goes to GND. With digits>1 multiplex DIG1..DIG4 and keep the refresh fast.

a4988.name: A4988 Stepper Driver
a4988.description: A4988 bipolar stepper motor driver (STEP/DIR). Pulse STEP to advance one step; DIR sets the direction; MS1-MS3 select microstepping. Outputs 1A/1B (coil A) and 2A/2B (coil B) to a stepper's A+/A-/B+/B- terminals.
a4988.notes: A4988 stepper driver: VDD=5V logic, VMOT=motor supply (with a 100uF capacitor across it), the GND pins to GND, STEP/DIR from GPIOs, ENABLE optional, MS1-3 set microstepping, 1A/1B/2A/2B to the stepper coils.

externalDriver.why: the stepper coils are driven by the A4988's own H-bridges, not by the board

analog-joystick.name: Analog Joystick
analog-joystick.notes: Analog joystick: VERT/HORZ to two analog pins, SEL is a push button (INPUT_PULLUP to GND). Use the pot interaction with a pin name to drive one axis.

arduino-mega.name: Arduino Mega
arduino-mega.why: only the Arduino Uno is supported as a build target right now

arduino-nano.name: Arduino Nano
arduino-nano.why: only the Arduino Uno is supported as a build target right now

arduino-uno.name: Arduino Uno
arduino-uno.why: the board is the project's `board` field, not a component

battery-9v.name: 9V Battery
battery-9v.description: PP3 / 6LR61 9V alkaline battery. Modelled as 9V DC with ~1.5Ω internal resistance.
battery-9v.notes: Battery: `+` is the supply rail, `−` the ground. Use it for loads a GPIO cannot drive (motors, relays, servos) and join the grounds.

battery-aa.name: AA Battery (1.5V)
battery-aa.description: AA alkaline cell. 1.5V, low ESR (~0.15Ω). Pair up for 3V/4.5V/6V packs.
battery-aa.notes: Battery: `+` is the supply rail, `−` the ground. Use it for loads a GPIO cannot drive (motors, relays, servos) and join the grounds.

battery-coin-cell.name: Coin Cell (CR2032, 3V)
battery-coin-cell.description: Lithium coin cell. 3V, high ESR (~10Ω) — limits peak current.
battery-coin-cell.notes: Battery: `+` is the supply rail, `−` the ground. Use it for loads a GPIO cannot drive (motors, relays, servos) and join the grounds.

biaxial-stepper.name: Biaxial Stepper
biaxial-stepper.notes: Two-phase stepper with two coils per phase: every coil pair goes to a driver channel.

externalDriver.why: stepper coils need H-bridge drivers, not GPIOs

big-sound-sensor.name: Big Sound Sensor
big-sound-sensor.notes: Sound sensor (big): AOUT is the audio envelope, DOUT a threshold output. Sample AOUT with analogRead.

bjt-2n2222.name: 2N2222 (NPN BJT)
bjt-2n2222.description: General-purpose NPN bipolar transistor. The go-to part for low-power switching and small-signal amplification.
bjt-2n2222.notes: NPN transistor: E to GND, load between +V and C, B driven through a base resistor (1k-10k) from a GPIO. That is how a GPIO switches anything bigger than an LED.

bjt-2n3055.name: 2N3055 (NPN Power BJT)
bjt-2n3055.description: Power NPN bipolar transistor. 15A / 60V / 115W TO-3 package. Classic audio amp output stage.
bjt-2n3055.notes: NPN transistor: E to GND, load between +V and C, B driven through a base resistor (1k-10k) from a GPIO. That is how a GPIO switches anything bigger than an LED.

bjt-2n3906.name: 2N3906 (PNP BJT)
bjt-2n3906.description: General-purpose PNP bipolar transistor. Complement of the 2N3904/2N2222.
bjt-2n3906.notes: PNP transistor: E to +V, load between C and GND, B to GND through a resistor to switch it on (a GPIO drives it LOW).

bjt-bc547.name: BC547 (NPN BJT)
bjt-bc547.description: Small-signal NPN bipolar transistor, European equivalent of 2N3904. High gain (~400).
bjt-bc547.notes: NPN transistor: E to GND, load between +V and C, B driven through a base resistor (1k-10k) from a GPIO. That is how a GPIO switches anything bigger than an LED.

bjt-bc557.name: BC557 (PNP BJT)
bjt-bc557.description: Small-signal PNP bipolar transistor. Complement of the BC547.
bjt-bc557.notes: PNP transistor: E to +V, load between C and GND, B to GND through a resistor to switch it on (a GPIO drives it LOW).

bmp280.name: BMP280 (Pressure + Temp)
bmp280.notes: BMP280 barometer over I2C: VCC=5V (module) or 3.3V, GND, SDA=A4, SCL=A5, address 0x76/0x77 (SDO picks it).

breadboard.name: Breadboard (full)
breadboard.description: 830-point solderless breadboard: 63 columns x two 5-hole banks (a-e / f-j) plus four full-length power rails. Holes in the same column strip or rail are electrically connected.
breadboard.why: prototyping boards are wiring aids: their rows are nets, not part pins, and the analysis works on direct wires

breadboard-mini.name: Breadboard Mini
breadboard-mini.description: 170-point mini solderless breadboard: 17 columns x two 5-hole banks (a-e / f-j), no power rails. Holes in the same column strip are electrically connected.
breadboard-mini.why: same as the full breadboard — the agent wires parts directly

buzzer.name: Buzzer
buzzer.description: Whether the buzzer is currently emitting a signal
buzzer.notes: Piezo buzzer: pin 1 to GND, pin 2 to a GPIO. Drive it with tone() (or analogWrite for volume on a PWM pin).

cap-100n.name: Cap. 100 nF
cap-100n.notes: Ceramic capacitor. Decoupling between a supply and GND; a timing capacitor on a GPIO must be charged through a resistor.

cap-100p.name: Cap. 100 pF
cap-100p.notes: Ceramic capacitor. Decoupling between a supply and GND; a timing capacitor on a GPIO must be charged through a resistor.

cap-10n.name: Cap. 10 nF
cap-10n.notes: Ceramic capacitor. Decoupling between a supply and GND; a timing capacitor on a GPIO must be charged through a resistor.

cap-10p.name: Cap. 10 pF
cap-10p.notes: Ceramic capacitor. Decoupling between a supply and GND; a timing capacitor on a GPIO must be charged through a resistor.

cap-1n.name: Cap. 1 nF
cap-1n.notes: Ceramic capacitor. Decoupling between a supply and GND; a timing capacitor on a GPIO must be charged through a resistor.

cap-1u.name: Cap. 1 µF
cap-1u.notes: Ceramic capacitor. Decoupling between a supply and GND; a timing capacitor on a GPIO must be charged through a resistor.

cap-22p.name: Cap. 22 pF
cap-22p.notes: Ceramic capacitor. Decoupling between a supply and GND; a timing capacitor on a GPIO must be charged through a resistor.

cap-elec-1000u.name: Electrolytic 1000 µF
cap-elec-1000u.notes: Electrolytic capacitor: `+` to the higher potential, `−` to GND. Never reverse it.

cap-elec-100u.name: Electrolytic 100 µF
cap-elec-100u.notes: Electrolytic capacitor: `+` to the higher potential, `−` to GND. Never reverse it.

cap-elec-10u.name: Electrolytic 10 µF
cap-elec-10u.notes: Electrolytic capacitor: `+` to the higher potential, `−` to GND. Never reverse it.

cap-elec-1u.name: Electrolytic 1 µF
cap-elec-1u.notes: Electrolytic capacitor: `+` to the higher potential, `−` to GND. Never reverse it.

cap-elec-470u.name: Electrolytic 470 µF
cap-elec-470u.notes: Electrolytic capacitor: `+` to the higher potential, `−` to GND. Never reverse it.

cap-elec-47u.name: Electrolytic 47 µF
cap-elec-47u.notes: Electrolytic capacitor: `+` to the higher potential, `−` to GND. Never reverse it.

capacitor.name: Cap. ceramic (custom)
capacitor.notes: Ceramic capacitor. Decoupling between a supply and GND; a timing capacitor on a GPIO must be charged through a resistor.

capacitor-electrolytic.name: Electrolytic Cap. (custom)
capacitor-electrolytic.notes: Electrolytic capacitor: `+` to the higher potential, `−` to GND. Never reverse it.

dht22.name: DHT22
dht22.notes: DHT22 temperature/humidity: VCC=5V, GND, SDA to any GPIO with a 10k pull-up to 5V, read at most every 2 s with the DHT library. The NC pin is unused.

diode.name: Diode (generic)
diode.description: Generic silicon diode. Vf ≈ 0.7 V. Use for textbook rectification examples.
diode.notes: Diode: anode (A) toward the driving side, cathode (C, the stripe) toward the load/rail. Flyback diodes go across inductive loads, reverse-biased.

diode-1n4007.name: 1N4007 (1 kV Rectifier)
diode-1n4007.description: 1 A / 1000 V silicon rectifier diode. Mains bridge rectifiers, back-EMF protection.
diode-1n4007.notes: Diode: anode (A) toward the driving side, cathode (C, the stripe) toward the load/rail. Flyback diodes go across inductive loads, reverse-biased.

diode-1n4148.name: 1N4148 (Small-Signal Diode)
diode-1n4148.description: Small-signal silicon diode. Fast switching, low capacitance. Go-to for logic-level protection.
diode-1n4148.notes: Diode: anode (A) toward the driving side, cathode (C, the stripe) toward the load/rail. Flyback diodes go across inductive loads, reverse-biased.

diode-1n5817.name: 1N5817 (Schottky 20V)
diode-1n5817.description: Schottky diode, 1 A / 20 V. Vf ≈ 0.32 V at 1 A. Used in low-drop rectification and reverse-polarity protection.
diode-1n5817.notes: Diode: anode (A) toward the driving side, cathode (C, the stripe) toward the load/rail. Flyback diodes go across inductive loads, reverse-biased.

diode-1n5819.name: 1N5819 (Schottky 40V)
diode-1n5819.description: Schottky diode, 1 A / 40 V. Higher breakdown than 1N5817, same low Vf.
diode-1n5819.notes: Diode: anode (A) toward the driving side, cathode (C, the stripe) toward the load/rail. Flyback diodes go across inductive loads, reverse-biased.

dip-switch-8.name: DIP Switch 8
dip-switch-8.notes: 8-way DIP switch: each Na-Nb pair is an independent SPST switch. Na to a GPIO with INPUT_PULLUP, Nb to GND is the usual wiring.

ds1307.name: DS1307
ds1307.notes: DS1307 RTC over I2C at 0x68: 5V, GND, SDA=A4, SCL=A5. SQW can clock an interrupt pin. Set the time with RTClib's adjust().

ds3231.name: DS3231 RTC
ds3231.notes: DS3231 RTC over I2C at 0x68: VCC=5V, GND, SDA=A4, SCL=A5. It also reports temperature.

epaper-1in54-bw.name: ePaper 1.54" (200×200, B/W)
epaper-1in54-bw.notes: E-paper over SPI (hardware SCK=13, MOSI=11 on the Uno; CS/DC/RST on free GPIOs). BUSY is an output from the panel. A full refresh takes seconds.

epaper-2in13-bw.name: ePaper 2.13" (250×122, B/W)
epaper-2in13-bw.notes: E-paper over SPI (hardware SCK=13, MOSI=11 on the Uno; CS/DC/RST on free GPIOs). BUSY is an output from the panel. A full refresh takes seconds.

epaper-2in13-bwr.name: ePaper 2.13" (250×122, B/W/Red)
epaper-2in13-bwr.notes: E-paper over SPI (hardware SCK=13, MOSI=11 on the Uno; CS/DC/RST on free GPIOs). BUSY is an output from the panel. A full refresh takes seconds.

epaper-2in9-bw.name: ePaper 2.9" (296×128, B/W)
epaper-2in9-bw.notes: E-paper over SPI (hardware SCK=13, MOSI=11 on the Uno; CS/DC/RST on free GPIOs). BUSY is an output from the panel. A full refresh takes seconds.

epaper-2in9-bwr.name: ePaper 2.9" (296×128, B/W/Red)
epaper-2in9-bwr.notes: E-paper over SPI (hardware SCK=13, MOSI=11 on the Uno; CS/DC/RST on free GPIOs). BUSY is an output from the panel. A full refresh takes seconds.

epaper-4in2-bw.name: ePaper 4.2" (400×300, B/W)
epaper-4in2-bw.notes: E-paper over SPI (hardware SCK=13, MOSI=11 on the Uno; CS/DC/RST on free GPIOs). BUSY is an output from the panel. A full refresh takes seconds.

epaper-5in65-7c.name: ePaper 5.65" (600×448, ACeP 7-colour)
epaper-5in65-7c.notes: E-paper over SPI (hardware SCK=13, MOSI=11 on the Uno; CS/DC/RST on free GPIOs). BUSY is an output from the panel. A full refresh takes seconds.

epaper-7in5-bw.name: ePaper 7.5" (800×480, B/W)
epaper-7in5-bw.notes: E-paper over SPI (hardware SCK=13, MOSI=11 on the Uno; CS/DC/RST on free GPIOs). BUSY is an output from the panel. A full refresh takes seconds.

flame-sensor.name: Flame Sensor
flame-sensor.notes: Flame sensor: AOUT is the analog intensity, DOUT a threshold output (usually active LOW).

flip-flop-d.name: D Flip-Flop
flip-flop-d.description: Edge-triggered D-type flip-flop. On rising edge of CLK, Q ← D. Digital simulation only (SPICE cannot do edge detection in .op analysis).
flip-flop-d.notes: Edge-triggered flip-flop: CLK and D/J/K/T are inputs, Q/Qbar outputs. Drive CLK from a GPIO and expect one state change per rising edge.

flip-flop-jk.name: JK Flip-Flop
flip-flop-jk.description: JK flip-flop. On rising CLK: J=0/K=0 hold, J=1/K=0 set, J=0/K=1 reset, J=1/K=1 toggle.
flip-flop-jk.notes: Edge-triggered flip-flop: CLK and D/J/K/T are inputs, Q/Qbar outputs. Drive CLK from a GPIO and expect one state change per rising edge.

flip-flop-t.name: T Flip-Flop
flip-flop-t.description: Toggle flip-flop. On rising CLK, Q ← Q ⊕ T (toggles when T=1). Useful for frequency dividers and counters.
flip-flop-t.notes: Edge-triggered flip-flop: CLK and D/J/K/T are inputs, Q/Qbar outputs. Drive CLK from a GPIO and expect one state change per rising edge.

franzininho.name: Franzininho
franzininho.why: only the Arduino Uno is supported as a build target right now

gas-sensor.name: Gas Sensor
gas-sensor.notes: Gas sensor: AOUT is the analog level, DOUT trips at the trimpot threshold. It needs a warm-up before readings settle.

gps-neo6m.name: GPS NEO-6M
gps-neo6m.notes: NEO-6M GPS: TX to a GPIO used as SoftwareSerial RX (RX to a GPIO used as TX if you send commands). 9600 baud NMEA.

hc-sr04.name: HC-SR04
hc-sr04.notes: HC-SR04 ultrasonic: TRIG gets a 10 us pulse from a GPIO, ECHO returns a pulse whose width is the distance (pulseIn; cm = width / 58).

heart-beat-sensor.name: Heart Beat Sensor
heart-beat-sensor.description: Optical heart-rate (pulse) sensor module. OUT carries a photoplethysmogram: read it with analogRead for the waveform, or with digitalRead for one pulse per beat. Set the rate with the bpm property or the sensor panel.
heart-beat-sensor.notes: Pulse sensor: OUT is an analog waveform, one peak per heartbeat. Threshold it in software to count beats per minute.

hx711.name: HX711
hx711.notes: HX711 load-cell amplifier: DT is the data output, SCK is clocked by the GPIO (HX711 library). Decode its own protocol — there is no sensor knob for it in the browser.

ic-74hc00.name: 74HC00 (Quad 2-input NAND)
ic-74hc00.description: Four 2-input NAND gates in one 14-pin DIP package. 74HC family (high-speed CMOS).
ic-74hc00.notes: 74HC logic IC: VCC to 5V, GND to GND, and an unused input must never float — tie it to a rail or drive it. Outputs (nY) can drive a GPIO input, or an LED through a series resistor.

ic-74hc02.name: 74HC02 (Quad 2-input NOR)
ic-74hc02.description: Four 2-input NOR gates in one 14-pin DIP package.
ic-74hc02.notes: 74HC logic IC: VCC to 5V, GND to GND, and an unused input must never float — tie it to a rail or drive it. Outputs (nY) can drive a GPIO input, or an LED through a series resistor.

ic-74hc04.name: 74HC04 (Hex Inverter)
ic-74hc04.description: Six NOT gates (inverters) in one 14-pin DIP package.
ic-74hc04.notes: 74HC logic IC: VCC to 5V, GND to GND, and an unused input must never float — tie it to a rail or drive it. Outputs (nY) can drive a GPIO input, or an LED through a series resistor.

ic-74hc08.name: 74HC08 (Quad 2-input AND)
ic-74hc08.description: Four 2-input AND gates in one 14-pin DIP package.
ic-74hc08.notes: 74HC logic IC: VCC to 5V, GND to GND, and an unused input must never float — tie it to a rail or drive it. Outputs (nY) can drive a GPIO input, or an LED through a series resistor.

ic-74hc14.name: 74HC14 (Hex Schmitt Inverter)
ic-74hc14.description: Six Schmitt-trigger inverters in one 14-pin DIP package. Provides input hysteresis — essential for debouncing noisy signals.
ic-74hc14.notes: 74HC logic IC: VCC to 5V, GND to GND, and an unused input must never float — tie it to a rail or drive it. Outputs (nY) can drive a GPIO input, or an LED through a series resistor.

ic-74hc32.name: 74HC32 (Quad 2-input OR)
ic-74hc32.description: Four 2-input OR gates in one 14-pin DIP package.
ic-74hc32.notes: 74HC logic IC: VCC to 5V, GND to GND, and an unused input must never float — tie it to a rail or drive it. Outputs (nY) can drive a GPIO input, or an LED through a series resistor.

ic-74hc86.name: 74HC86 (Quad 2-input XOR)
ic-74hc86.description: Four 2-input XOR gates in one 14-pin DIP package.
ic-74hc86.notes: 74HC logic IC: VCC to 5V, GND to GND, and an unused input must never float — tie it to a rail or drive it. Outputs (nY) can drive a GPIO input, or an LED through a series resistor.

ili9341.name: ILI9341
ili9341.notes: ILI9341 TFT over SPI: SCK=13, MOSI=11, CS/DC/RST on free GPIOs, MISO optional, LED (backlight) to 5V or a PWM pin. 3.3V logic — level-shift if you power it from 5V.

ind-100u.name: Inductor 100 µH
ind-100u.notes: Inductor. A GPIO cannot drive one directly — use a transistor with a flyback diode.

ind-10m.name: Inductor 10 mH
ind-10m.notes: Inductor. A GPIO cannot drive one directly — use a transistor with a flyback diode.

ind-1m.name: Inductor 1 mH
ind-1m.notes: Inductor. A GPIO cannot drive one directly — use a transistor with a flyback diode.

inductor.name: Inductor (custom)
inductor.notes: Inductor. A GPIO cannot drive one directly — use a transistor with a flyback diode.

ir-receiver.name: IR Receiver
ir-receiver.notes: IR receiver module: DAT to any GPIO (the carrier is already demodulated). Decode with the IRremote library.

ir-remote.name: IR Remote
ir-remote.notes: IR remote handset: no wires — place it next to an IR receiver and stimulate the RECEIVER with address/command to send a frame.

junction.name: Junction
junction.description: Wire junction node - connects a wire to another wire so a shared rail (GND, VCC) can be one wire with taps. Created by dropping a wire end onto an existing wire or with the node tool; hidden from the picker.
junction.why: a junction merges wires and has no pins to reason about; express nets with direct wires instead

ks2e-m-dc5.name: KS2E-M-DC5
ks2e-m-dc5.notes: Two-pole relay: COIL1/COIL2 is the coil (drive it through a transistor); P1 with NO1/NC1 and P2 with NO2/NC2 are the two isolated poles.

externalDriver.why: a relay coil draws more current than a GPIO can source and needs a flyback diode

ky-040.name: KY-040 Rotary Encoder
ky-040.description: KY-040 incremental rotary encoder with push-button. Turning the knob outputs quadrature pulses on CLK and DT (direction = which leads); the shaft press drives an active-low SW. Reads from any board's GPIO.
ky-040.notes: Rotary encoder with a push button: CLK/DT are the quadrature outputs (pull-ups are on the module), SW is the shaft button. Read CLK in an interrupt and SW with INPUT_PULLUP.

lcd1602.name: LCD1602
lcd1602.notes: Character LCD in 4-bit parallel mode: RS, E and D4-D7 (6 GPIOs), VDD=5V, VSS=GND, K=GND (backlight cathode), V0 to a 10k contrast pot. Use the LiquidCrystal library; wire D0-D3 only for 8-bit mode.

lcd1602-i2c.name: LCD 16x2 (I2C)
lcd1602-i2c.notes: I2C character LCD backpack: VCC=5V, GND, SDA=A4, SCL=A5 (Uno), address 0x27/0x3F. Construct LiquidCrystal_I2C with that address.

lcd2004.name: LCD2004
lcd2004.notes: Character LCD in 4-bit parallel mode: RS, E and D4-D7 (6 GPIOs), VDD=5V, VSS=GND, K=GND (backlight cathode), V0 to a 10k contrast pot. Use the LiquidCrystal library; wire D0-D3 only for 8-bit mode.

lcd2004-i2c.name: LCD 20x4 (I2C)
lcd2004-i2c.notes: I2C character LCD backpack: VCC=5V, GND, SDA=A4, SCL=A5 (Uno), address 0x27/0x3F. Construct LiquidCrystal_I2C with that address.

led.name: LED
led.notes: LED: A=anode (long leg), C=cathode. Always in series with a 220-1000 ohm resistor; use a PWM pin (3,5,6,9,10,11) for brightness.

led-bar-graph.name: Led Bar Graph
led-bar-graph.notes: 10-segment bar graph: C1..C10 are the cathodes (GND), A1..A10 the anodes, each needing its own series resistor.

led-ring.name: LED Ring
led-ring.notes: WS2812 ring: 5V, GND, DIN from a GPIO. Set the pixel-count property to the ring size.

logic-gate-and.name: AND Gate
logic-gate-and.description: 2-input AND logic gate. Output Y = A · B.
logic-gate-and.notes: Logic gate: inputs A..D must be driven by GPIOs (or another output), Y is the output. The model has no power pins — never leave an input floating.

logic-gate-and-3.name: AND Gate (3-input)
logic-gate-and-3.description: 3-input AND gate. Output Y = A · B · C.
logic-gate-and-3.notes: Logic gate: inputs A..D must be driven by GPIOs (or another output), Y is the output. The model has no power pins — never leave an input floating.

logic-gate-and-4.name: AND Gate (4-input)
logic-gate-and-4.notes: Logic gate: inputs A..D must be driven by GPIOs (or another output), Y is the output. The model has no power pins — never leave an input floating.

logic-gate-nand.name: NAND Gate
logic-gate-nand.description: 2-input NAND logic gate. Output Y = NOT(A · B).
logic-gate-nand.notes: Logic gate: inputs A..D must be driven by GPIOs (or another output), Y is the output. The model has no power pins — never leave an input floating.

logic-gate-nand-3.name: NAND Gate (3-input)
logic-gate-nand-3.notes: Logic gate: inputs A..D must be driven by GPIOs (or another output), Y is the output. The model has no power pins — never leave an input floating.

logic-gate-nand-4.name: NAND Gate (4-input)
logic-gate-nand-4.notes: Logic gate: inputs A..D must be driven by GPIOs (or another output), Y is the output. The model has no power pins — never leave an input floating.

logic-gate-nor.name: NOR Gate
logic-gate-nor.description: 2-input NOR logic gate. Output Y = NOT(A + B).
logic-gate-nor.notes: Logic gate: inputs A..D must be driven by GPIOs (or another output), Y is the output. The model has no power pins — never leave an input floating.

logic-gate-nor-3.name: NOR Gate (3-input)
logic-gate-nor-3.notes: Logic gate: inputs A..D must be driven by GPIOs (or another output), Y is the output. The model has no power pins — never leave an input floating.

logic-gate-nor-4.name: NOR Gate (4-input)
logic-gate-nor-4.notes: Logic gate: inputs A..D must be driven by GPIOs (or another output), Y is the output. The model has no power pins — never leave an input floating.

logic-gate-not.name: NOT Gate (Inverter)
logic-gate-not.notes: Logic gate: inputs A..D must be driven by GPIOs (or another output), Y is the output. The model has no power pins — never leave an input floating.

logic-gate-or.name: OR Gate
logic-gate-or.description: 2-input OR logic gate. Output Y = A + B.
logic-gate-or.notes: Logic gate: inputs A..D must be driven by GPIOs (or another output), Y is the output. The model has no power pins — never leave an input floating.

logic-gate-or-3.name: OR Gate (3-input)
logic-gate-or-3.description: 3-input OR gate. Output Y = A + B + C.
logic-gate-or-3.notes: Logic gate: inputs A..D must be driven by GPIOs (or another output), Y is the output. The model has no power pins — never leave an input floating.

logic-gate-or-4.name: OR Gate (4-input)
logic-gate-or-4.notes: Logic gate: inputs A..D must be driven by GPIOs (or another output), Y is the output. The model has no power pins — never leave an input floating.

logic-gate-xnor.name: XNOR Gate
logic-gate-xnor.description: 2-input XNOR logic gate. Output Y = NOT(A ⊕ B).
logic-gate-xnor.notes: Logic gate: inputs A..D must be driven by GPIOs (or another output), Y is the output. The model has no power pins — never leave an input floating.

logic-gate-xor.name: XOR Gate
logic-gate-xor.description: 2-input XOR logic gate. Output Y = A ⊕ B.
logic-gate-xor.notes: Logic gate: inputs A..D must be driven by GPIOs (or another output), Y is the output. The model has no power pins — never leave an input floating.

membrane-keypad.name: Membrane Keypad
membrane-keypad.notes: 4x4 matrix keypad: R1-R4 rows, C1-C4 columns (8 GPIOs). Scan the rows and read the columns with INPUT_PULLUP. It cannot be auto-stimulated in the browser.

microsd-card.name: microSD Card
microsd-card.notes: microSD over SPI: SCK=13, DI=MOSI=11, DO=MISO=12, CS on GPIO 10 (the SD library default) or another pin. 3.3V supply and logic.

mosfet-2n7000.name: 2N7000 (N-MOSFET)
mosfet-2n7000.description: Logic-level N-channel MOSFET. Vth ≈ 1.6 V, fully enhanced at 3.3 V — perfect for GPIO-driven load switching.
mosfet-2n7000.notes: MOSFET: S to GND (N-channel), load between +V and D, G through a 10-220 ohm gate resistor, plus a 10k pull-down from G to S so it cannot float on.

mosfet-fqp27p06.name: FQP27P06 (P-MOSFET)
mosfet-fqp27p06.description: Logic-level P-channel MOSFET. Suitable for 3.3V / 5V gate drive.
mosfet-fqp27p06.notes: MOSFET: S to GND (N-channel), load between +V and D, G through a 10-220 ohm gate resistor, plus a 10k pull-down from G to S so it cannot float on.

mosfet-irf540.name: IRF540 (N-MOSFET Power)
mosfet-irf540.description: Power N-channel MOSFET. Vth ≈ 3 V (needs 10 V for full enhancement), 33 A / 100 V, R_DS(on) ≈ 77 mΩ. Classic motor / solenoid driver.
mosfet-irf540.notes: MOSFET: S to GND (N-channel), load between +V and D, G through a 10-220 ohm gate resistor, plus a 10k pull-down from G to S so it cannot float on.

mosfet-irf9540.name: IRF9540 (P-MOSFET)
mosfet-irf9540.description: Power P-channel MOSFET. Used for high-side load switching with logic input.
mosfet-irf9540.notes: MOSFET: S to GND (N-channel), load between +V and D, G through a 10-220 ohm gate resistor, plus a 10k pull-down from G to S so it cannot float on.

motor-driver-l293d.name: L293D (Dual H-Bridge Motor Driver)
motor-driver-l293d.description: Dual H-bridge motor driver IC. Each channel: EN, IN1, IN2 drive OUT1/OUT2 with the motor supply voltage (VCC2). Rated 600 mA continuous / 1.2 A peak per channel.
motor-driver-l293d.notes: L293D dual H-bridge: VCC1=5V logic, VCC2=motor supply, the GND pins to GND. IN1-4 choose the direction, EN1/EN2 take PWM for speed, OUT1-4 go to the motors.

mpu6050.name: MPU6050
mpu6050.notes: MPU6050 IMU over I2C: VCC=5V (module), GND, SDA=A4, SCL=A5, address 0x68/0x69 (AD0 picks it). INT is optional.

neopixel.name: Neopixel
neopixel.notes: WS2812 strip: 5V, GND, data into DIN (a 300-500 ohm series resistor and a large electrolytic across the supply are good practice). Drive it with Adafruit_NeoPixel; never power a long strip from the Uno's 5V pin.

neopixel-matrix.name: NeoPixel Matrix
neopixel-matrix.notes: WS2812 matrix: VCC=5V, GND, DIN from a GPIO through a series resistor; DOUT chains on to the next panel.

ntc-temperature-sensor.name: NTC Temperature Sensor
ntc-temperature-sensor.notes: NTC thermistor module: OUT to an analog pin; the voltage tracks temperature.

opamp-ideal.name: Ideal Op-Amp
opamp-ideal.description: Idealized operational amplifier. Infinite gain, infinite input impedance, no saturation. Use for textbook circuits where real-chip limitations are irrelevant.
opamp-ideal.notes: Op-amp (the model has no supply pins): OUT swings between the rails. No feedback network is required, but no input may float.

opamp-lm324.name: LM324 (Quad Op-Amp)
opamp-lm324.description: Quad single-supply op-amp. Same electrical spec as LM358, four channels per package.
opamp-lm324.notes: Op-amp (the model has no supply pins): OUT swings between the rails. No feedback network is required, but no input may float.

opamp-lm358.name: LM358 (Dual Op-Amp)
opamp-lm358.description: Dual single-supply op-amp. Output swings close to both rails. Ideal for MCU-powered signal conditioning.
opamp-lm358.notes: Op-amp (the model has no supply pins): OUT swings between the rails. No feedback network is required, but no input may float.

opamp-lm741.name: LM741 (Op-Amp)
opamp-lm741.description: Classic general-purpose op-amp. Requires ~1.5V of headroom from each supply rail. Used in didactic circuits.
opamp-lm741.notes: Op-amp (the model has no supply pins): OUT swings between the rails. No feedback network is required, but no input may float.

opamp-tl072.name: TL072 (JFET Op-Amp)
opamp-tl072.description: JFET-input dual op-amp. Very high input impedance, low noise — audio and instrumentation.
opamp-tl072.notes: Op-amp (the model has no supply pins): OUT swings between the rails. No feedback network is required, but no input may float.

opto-4n25.name: 4N25 (Optocoupler)
opto-4n25.description: Single-channel optocoupler with IR LED + phototransistor. CTR ≈ 50%. Provides galvanic isolation between two circuits.
opto-4n25.notes: Optocoupler: drive AN through a 220-1k resistor (CAT to GND) and use COL/EMIT as the isolated switch on the other side.

opto-pc817.name: PC817 (Optocoupler)
opto-pc817.description: Single-channel optocoupler. CTR 80–600% (typ. 100%). Higher drive than 4N25, commonly used for MCU-to-mains isolation.
opto-pc817.notes: Optocoupler: drive AN through a 220-1k resistor (CAT to GND) and use COL/EMIT as the isolated switch on the other side.

photodiode.name: Photodiode
photodiode.description: Light-sensitive diode. Reverse current proportional to illumination. Property: lux (ambient light intensity).
photodiode.notes: Photodiode: reverse-biased (C toward the higher potential) it produces a small photocurrent — amplify it, or use an LDR module.

photoresistor-sensor.name: Photoresistor Sensor
photoresistor-sensor.notes: LDR module: AO is an analog light level (A0-A5), DO is a comparator output whose threshold comes from its trimpot.

pir-motion-sensor.name: PIR Motion Sensor
pir-motion-sensor.notes: PIR motion module: OUT goes HIGH while motion is detected. Give it a second to settle after power-up.

potentiometer.name: Potentiometer
potentiometer.notes: Potentiometer: VCC=5V, GND=GND, SIG to an analog pin (A0-A5). Read it with analogRead — the wiper is a voltage divider, so it cannot be read as a digital pin.

power-supply.name: Regulated Power Supply
power-supply.description: Bench DC/AC power supply with optional current limit. DC mode for fixed rails (5V, 12V, etc.); AC mode for sine sources. Visually shares the signal-generator chassis so no new Web Component is needed. The current limit is enforced by the circuit verifier — if any load pulls more than the configured amperage, Run is blocked with a 'source-overload' warning, mimicking a real bench supply's foldback behavior.
power-supply.notes: Bench supply: GND is the ground rail, SIG is the regulated output (set its voltage with the property). Use it instead of the Uno's 5V pin for anything that draws real current.

pushbutton.name: Pushbutton
pushbutton.notes: Momentary pushbutton. It has TWO contacts and each contact has two legs joined inside the part: contact 1 = 1.l + 1.r, contact 2 = 2.l + 2.r; pressing closes contact 1 to contact 2. Wire the GPIO to ONE contact and GND to the OTHER (e.g. GPIO to 1.l, GND to 2.l) and read it with pinMode(pin, INPUT_PULLUP) - it reads LOW while pressed. GPIO on 1.l with GND on 1.r is both legs of the SAME contact: a dead short that ties the pin to GND and never switches.

pushbutton-6mm.name: Pushbutton 6mm
pushbutton-6mm.notes: Panel-mount pushbutton — same contacts as the standard one: contact 1 = 1.l + 1.r, contact 2 = 2.l + 2.r (legs of one contact are joined inside). GPIO (INPUT_PULLUP) on one contact and GND on the OTHER (GPIO to 1.l, GND to 2.l); GPIO on 1.l with GND on 1.r is the same contact, a dead short.

reg-7805.name: 7805 (+5V Linear Regulator)
reg-7805.description: Fixed +5V linear regulator, 1A, TO-220. Dropout ≈ 2V. Classic MCU power supply.
reg-7805.notes: Linear regulator: VIN from an unregulated supply, VOUT is the regulated rail for the rest of the circuit. Never wire VOUT (or VIN) to a GPIO.

reg-7812.name: 7812 (+12V Linear Regulator)
reg-7812.description: Fixed +12V linear regulator, 1A, TO-220. Dropout ≈ 2V. Motor drivers, fan supplies.
reg-7812.notes: Linear regulator: VIN from an unregulated supply, VOUT is the regulated rail for the rest of the circuit. Never wire VOUT (or VIN) to a GPIO.

reg-7905.name: 7905 (−5V Linear Regulator)
reg-7905.description: Fixed −5V linear regulator, 1A, TO-220. Negative-rail complement of the 7805.
reg-7905.notes: Linear regulator: VIN from an unregulated supply, VOUT is the regulated rail for the rest of the circuit. Never wire VOUT (or VIN) to a GPIO.

reg-lm317.name: LM317 (Adjustable Linear Regulator)
reg-lm317.description: Adjustable +1.25V to +37V linear regulator. V_out = 1.25·(1 + R2/R1). Versatile workhorse.
reg-lm317.notes: Adjustable regulator: VIN from the supply, ADJ sets the output, VOUT is the regulated rail. Never wire VOUT to a GPIO.

relay.name: Relay (SPDT)
relay.description: 5-pin single-pole double-throw electromechanical relay. Coil drives SPDT contacts with native switch hysteresis. Optional integrated flyback diode.
relay.notes: Relay: COIL+/COIL- is the coil — drive it through a transistor (with a flyback diode), never straight from a GPIO. COM/NO/NC are the isolated contacts that switch your load.

externalDriver.why: a relay coil draws far more current than a GPIO can source and kicks back when it switches off

resistor.name: Resistor (custom)
resistor.notes: Two-terminal resistor. `value` in ohms (100..1e7). In series with an LED use 220-1000; as a pull-up/pull-down 1k-100k; as a base resistor 1k-10k.

resistor-100k.name: Resistor 100 kΩ
resistor-100k.notes: Two-terminal resistor. `value` in ohms (100..1e7). In series with an LED use 220-1000; as a pull-up/pull-down 1k-100k; as a base resistor 1k-10k.

resistor-10k.name: Resistor 10 kΩ
resistor-10k.notes: Two-terminal resistor. `value` in ohms (100..1e7). In series with an LED use 220-1000; as a pull-up/pull-down 1k-100k; as a base resistor 1k-10k.

resistor-1k.name: Resistor 1 kΩ
resistor-1k.notes: Two-terminal resistor. `value` in ohms (100..1e7). In series with an LED use 220-1000; as a pull-up/pull-down 1k-100k; as a base resistor 1k-10k.

resistor-1m.name: Resistor 1 MΩ
resistor-1m.notes: Two-terminal resistor. `value` in ohms (100..1e7). In series with an LED use 220-1000; as a pull-up/pull-down 1k-100k; as a base resistor 1k-10k.

resistor-220.name: Resistor 220 Ω
resistor-220.notes: Two-terminal resistor. `value` in ohms (100..1e7). In series with an LED use 220-1000; as a pull-up/pull-down 1k-100k; as a base resistor 1k-10k.

resistor-22k.name: Resistor 22 kΩ
resistor-22k.notes: Two-terminal resistor. `value` in ohms (100..1e7). In series with an LED use 220-1000; as a pull-up/pull-down 1k-100k; as a base resistor 1k-10k.

resistor-2k2.name: Resistor 2.2 kΩ
resistor-2k2.notes: Two-terminal resistor. `value` in ohms (100..1e7). In series with an LED use 220-1000; as a pull-up/pull-down 1k-100k; as a base resistor 1k-10k.

resistor-330.name: Resistor 330 Ω
resistor-330.notes: Two-terminal resistor. `value` in ohms (100..1e7). In series with an LED use 220-1000; as a pull-up/pull-down 1k-100k; as a base resistor 1k-10k.

resistor-470.name: Resistor 470 Ω
resistor-470.notes: Two-terminal resistor. `value` in ohms (100..1e7). In series with an LED use 220-1000; as a pull-up/pull-down 1k-100k; as a base resistor 1k-10k.

resistor-47k.name: Resistor 47 kΩ
resistor-47k.notes: Two-terminal resistor. `value` in ohms (100..1e7). In series with an LED use 220-1000; as a pull-up/pull-down 1k-100k; as a base resistor 1k-10k.

resistor-4k7.name: Resistor 4.7 kΩ
resistor-4k7.notes: Two-terminal resistor. `value` in ohms (100..1e7). In series with an LED use 220-1000; as a pull-up/pull-down 1k-100k; as a base resistor 1k-10k.

rgb-led.name: RGB Led
rgb-led.notes: RGB LED with a common cathode (COM to GND): R/G/B are three separate LEDs, each needing its own 150-330 ohm resistor. PWM each channel to mix colours.

rotary-dialer.name: Rotary Dialer
rotary-dialer.notes: Pulse-dial telephone dial: PULSE gives one pulse per digit, DIAL marks that a digit is being dialled. Count pulses in an interrupt.

servo.name: Servo
servo.description: The angle of the servo (0-180 degrees)
servo.notes: Hobby servo: PWM (the signal) on a PWM-capable pin (3,5,6,9,10,11), V+ and GND to a 5V supply that can deliver the stall current. Servo.h disables analogWrite on pins 9 and 10. Expect ~50 Hz pulses.

signal-generator.name: Signal Generator
signal-generator.description: Benchtop AC/DC signal source. Sine, square, or DC output. Configurable frequency, amplitude, DC offset.
signal-generator.notes: Signal generator: GND plus a SIG output you can configure (waveform, frequency, amplitude). Feed it into a GPIO (or a load with a safe amplitude).

slide-potentiometer.name: Slide Potentiometer
slide-potentiometer.notes: Slide potentiometer: the same three terminals as a rotary pot (VCC, GND, SIG to an analog pin).

slide-switch.name: Slide Switch
slide-switch.notes: SPDT slide switch: 2 is the common, 1 and 3 the throws. Common to a GPIO (INPUT_PULLUP), one throw to GND — or use both throws as a selector. The `value` property is the resting position.

small-sound-sensor.name: Small Sound Sensor
small-sound-sensor.notes: Sound sensor (small): the same pins as the big one, lower gain.

ssd1306.name: SSD1306 OLED
ssd1306.notes: SSD1306 128x64 OLED. I2C mode: CLK=SCL (A5), DATA=SDA (A4), the 3V3/VIN pin to a supply, address 0x3C. SPI mode uses CS/DC/RST instead — pick one mode and wire it completely.

ssd1306-i2c-4pin.name: SSD1306 OLED (I2C, 4-pin)
ssd1306-i2c-4pin.notes: 4-pin I2C OLED (VCC, GND, SDA=A4, SCL=A5), address 0x3C — the easiest display to add to a project.

stepper-motor.name: Stepper Motor
stepper-motor.notes: Bipolar stepper: A+/A-/B+/B- are the two coils. They go to a driver, never to the board.

externalDriver.why: a stepper coil cannot be driven from a GPIO; it needs a driver (A4988 or L293D)

tilt-switch.name: Tilt Switch
tilt-switch.notes: Tilt sensor module: OUT changes level when tilted. Read it with INPUT_PULLUP (check the module's polarity).

zener-1n4733.name: 1N4733 (5.1 V Zener)
zener-1n4733.description: 5.1 V Zener diode, 1 W. Voltage reference / regulator / ESD clamp.
zener-1n4733.notes: Diode: anode (A) toward the driving side, cathode (C, the stripe) toward the load/rail. Flyback diodes go across inductive loads, reverse-biased.
